breaking_changes: GET /api/v1/system-stats now reports the scalar gpu_percent and vram_gb fields for the primary GPU by total memory instead of the GPU with the highest utilization — on multi-GPU systems the numbers meaningfully change and existing dashboards or alerting based on those fields will see different values.

Models gated behind a guest-tier backend are now hidden from GET /v1/models?show_all=true and return model_not_supported on pull until the guest backend is installed — existing setups that relied on the model being visible without the backend will see them disappear.

checklist.author: @jeremyfowers
checklist.text: Open the Lemonade website news page and confirm the AnythingLLM entry displays the correct title ('Why AnythingLLM is moving from Ollama to Lemonade and llama.cpp'), date (October 13, 2026), description, and that the link resolves to anythingllm.com.

evidence.blockers: Two P0 items must pass: backend process lifecycle with real backend binaries (0c8169f), and guest backend model gating (65b0518). If either fails, the release cannot ship — broken process management blocks all backends, and broken gating blocks model installation on ROCm platforms.
evidence.breaking_changes: Two breaking changes identified: system-stats GPU selection behavior changes on multi-GPU systems (metrics now reflect primary GPU by memory rather than highest utilization), and guest backend gating that hides models until the guest backend is installed. Both have migration paths — the former requires dashboard consumers to check primary_gpu_id and the gpus array; the latter requires users to install the required guest backend before the model becomes available.
evidence.coverage: Reviewed 18 commits spanning v2026.42.1..f2208e4, covering the full range of the release bucket. All 14 to-dos from the commit reviews have been rated. Coverage includes backend lifecycle refactoring, image editing features, GPU telemetry, benchmark CLI, model discovery, version pin updates, test infrastructure, build system, and documentation.
evidence.manual_testing: Real backend end-to-end through start_server() path (0c8169f-1). Multi-reference image editing with actual image files (cf146ec-1). Guest backend install and model pull on ROCm hardware (65b0518-1). FLM inference on NPU hardware (0163739-1). System stats with mixed GPU hardware (2599015-1, 2599015-2). Live streaming throughput with active requests (d9ac446-1). Bench CLI with a local model (0a1477f-1).
evidence.security: No security concerns observed. The NVML DLL loading path on Windows was fixed during review (LoadLibraryExA with SEARCH_SYSTEM32 mitigates hijacking). Backend process management follows existing safe patterns. No new credential handling, network calls, or supply-chain changes.
